title: Exotic Perfume
text:
When I close my eyes beneath the autumn sun

And breathe the aroma of your warm breast,

Happy shores take shape before me,

Dazzled by the fires of an implacable sun.


A lazy island where Nature

Produces singular trees and most savory fruits,

Men displaying agile, slender bodies,

And women with eyes where wonder is painted.


Guided by your aroma toward magical climates,

I see a harbor filled with sails and masts

Still wearied by the marine swell,


While the light perfume of the tamarind,

Circulating in the air and dilating my nostrils,

Mingles in my soul with the sailors' song.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the beloved's scent as the route into tropical shore, harbor, tamarind, and sailors' song.

title: The Wine of the Solitary Man
text:
The singular gaze of a gallant woman

That reaches us like the white light

The moon might send to the trembling lake

When it wishes to bathe its indolent beauty;


The last coins a gambler owns;

A lustful kiss from skinny Adeline;

The echoes of warm, enervating music,

Like the distant cry of human suffering,


None of all that is worth, oh deep bottle,

The penetrating balm that your fertile belly

Offers to the overwhelmed poet's heart;


You dispense to him life, youth, and hope

—And pride, that defense against all misery

That makes us triumphant and like gods.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the poem's comparison of sensual pleasures with wine's proud consolation.

title: The Bad Monk
text:
Ancient cloisters on their broad walls

Unfold holy Truth in paintings,

Whose effect, warming pious entrails,

Tempers the coldness of their austerity.


In days when Christ's seeds were flowering,

More than one illustrious monk, now little cited,

Taking the cemetery for a workshop,

Glorified Death with simplicity.


—My soul is a tomb which, worst of cenobites,

From eternity I traverse and inhabit;

Nothing beautifies the walls of this hateful cloister.


Oh idle monk! When shall I know how to make

From the living spectacle of my sad misery

The work of my hands and the love of my eyes?
editorial_note: The translation keeps the soul-as-cloister conceit and the failure to turn misery into sacred art.

title: The Fountain of Blood
text:
Sometimes I feel my blood running in waves,

just like a fountain of rhythmic sobs;

I hear it run in long murmurs,

but in vain I feel myself to find the wound.


Through the city, like a closed field,

it goes transforming stones into islets,

slaking the thirst of every creature,

and coloring all nature red.


Often I have asked these wines

to calm for a single day the terror that gnaws me;

wine makes the gaze clearer and the ear keener.


I have sought in love a dream of oblivion;

but for me love is a prickling bed,

made to give those cruel women drink.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the unlocated wound, the city flooded with blood, and the failed consolations of wine and love.

title: On "Tasso in Prison"
text:
In his cell, the poet, ragged and ill,

Holding a manuscript beneath his convulsive foot,

Contemplates with a gaze flooded by panic

The stairway of vertigo where his soul sinks down.


The enervating laughter that populates the prison

Drags his reason toward the absurd and strange;

Doubt surrounds him, and ridiculous Fear,

Hateful and multiform, circles around him.


This genius shut inside an unhealthy den,

Those grimaces and cries, specters whose mutinous

Swarm turns behind his ears,


The dreamer whom horror has awakened,

Such is your emblem, Soul of dark dreams,

That drowns Reality within its four walls.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the imprisoned Tasso image as an emblem for the soul trapped among dreams, fear, and reality.
